data.content_ref: inline:The target claims the shown-to-fail-first installation establishes the test as a sufficiency condition (acceptance conditional on failure being impossible), but the 3-of-26 result shows the opposite: the ritual is insufficient to guarantee the constraint holds. Compile.py lost 1/9 mutations despite the installation, while ordinarily-guarded modules lost 4/4 to 6/7. If the test truly constrained the subject via a sufficiency condition, the installation should have been sufficient to prevent mutation loss across all modules. The variable success rate (3/26 vs 4/4-6/7) demonstrates that the test does not set a fixed boundary that the subject cannot cross. Instead, the test's constraining power varies by module in ways the sufficiency claim cannot explain. The mechanism claims the boundary was 'set too narrowly' for compile.py, but this concedes that the sufficiency condition failed: if the boundary can be set too narrowly while the installation ritual remains the same, then the installation does not turn the test into a sufficiency condition. The condition the target identifies is therefore not sufficient for constraint.
